learning_objectives: Explain what tokens are, how tokenization works, and why they are crucial for LLM performance, cost, and data processing.
outline: The role of Tokens in Chunking

slides.title: Title Slide: Understanding Tokens
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Understanding **Tokens**.
slides.image_prompt: Title slide with 'Understanding Tokens' prominently displayed, with subtle background graphics related to data processing or AI.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
content: See why **tokens** are crucial for **LLM** performance.
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn what **tokens** are.
You will understand how **tokenization** works.
You will also see why **tokens** are crucial for **LLM** performance.
This includes **context windows**, cost, and **chunking**.
slides.image_prompt: Learning objectives slide with bullet points and icons representing learning (lightbulb), understanding (brain), and importance (exclamation mark).

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have a basic understanding of **LLMs**.
slides.image_prompt: Prerequisites slide with text 'Basic understanding of LLMs' and an icon of a person thinking or studying.

slides.title: LLMs and Tokens
content: They break text into smaller pieces called **tokens**.
slides.narration:
Have you ever wondered how an **LLM** reads text?
It doesn't read words like we do.
Instead, it breaks text into smaller pieces.
These pieces are called **tokens**.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a human reading a book with words, contrasted with an AI brain processing abstract data blocks labeled 'tokens' from text input.

slides.title: What is a Tokenizer?
content: It splits raw text into sub-word **tokens**.
slides.narration:
A **tokenizer** is a special tool.
Think of it as the **LLM's** dictionary.
It splits your raw text into these sub-word **tokens**.
This is what the model truly understands.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram showing an input text box, an arrow pointing to a 'Tokenizer' machine icon, and then multiple smaller blocks labeled 'tokens' as output. A dictionary icon can be nearby.

slides.title: Tokenization Example: Simple Word
slides.narration:
Let's see an example of **tokenization**.
A simple word like "**The**" might be one **token**.
The **tokenizer** keeps it as a single unit.
Observe this on the screen.
slides.image_prompt: Screen showing an input box with 'The' and an output box showing a single block labeled 'The' as a token.

slides.title: Tokenization Example: Complex Word
slides.narration:
But a complex word is different.
Take "**Tokenization**" for instance.
It might be broken into three **tokens**.
Like "Token", "iz", and "ation".
This is how **LLMs** process complex words.
slides.image_prompt: Screen showing an input box with 'Tokenization' and an output box showing three separate blocks labeled 'Token', 'iz', and 'ation' as tokens.

slides.title: Why Tokens Matter
slides.narration:
So, why should you care about **tokens**?
They are very important for many reasons.
They impact how **LLMs** work.
Let's explore some key areas.
slides.image_prompt: A large question mark icon surrounded by smaller icons representing memory (brain), money (coin stack), and data processing (gears).

slides.title: Tokens and Context Windows
content: It's measured in a fixed number of **tokens** (e.g., 8,192).
This is the limit for your **prompt** and retrieved documents.
slides.narration:
First, consider **Context Windows**.
This is like an **LLM's** short-term memory.
It is measured in a fixed number of **tokens**.
For example, 8,192 **tokens**.
This is the maximum "context" you can give it.
This includes your **prompt** and any retrieved documents.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic of a computer monitor displaying a window. Inside the window are multiple small, identical slots or blocks, with a counter showing '8,192 tokens' and an arrow pointing to 'Context Window'.

slides.title: Tokens and Cost
slides.narration:
Next, let's talk about cost.
**API** providers charge you per **token**.
So, more **tokens** mean higher costs.
An efficient system uses fewer **tokens**.
This saves you money.
slides.image_prompt: A calculator or billing interface showing 'Cost per token' and a graph illustrating cost increasing with the number of tokens. A money bag icon is also visible.

slides.title: Tokens and RAG Efficiency
content: This makes **RAG** systems dramatically cheaper to run.
slides.narration:
For example, systems like **GraphRAG** are efficient.
They required 26% to 97% fewer **tokens**.
This makes them much cheaper to run.
It's a big saving.
slides.image_prompt: Bar chart comparing 'Standard RAG' vs 'GraphRAG' with 'Token Usage' on the Y-axis, showing GraphRAG's bar significantly lower. A dollar sign or cost reduction icon can be included.

slides.title: Tokens and Chunking
content: Breaking documents into smaller pieces is essential for **LLMs**.
slides.narration:
Finally, **tokens** are key for **chunking**.
When we process long documents, we "chunk" them.
We break them into smaller, manageable pieces.
These pieces are then sent to the **LLM**.
**Token** count helps define these chunks.
slides.image_prompt: An icon of a large document breaking into several smaller, uniform blocks labeled 'chunks' or 'token chunks', with arrows pointing towards an LLM icon.

slides.title: Summary
content: **Tokenization** is the process of splitting text.
slides.narration:
With this, we come to the end of this tutorial.
Let us summarise.
We learned what **tokens** are.
And how **tokenization** works.
We also saw why **tokens** are important for **LLM** performance.
They impact **context windows**, cost, and **chunking**.
slides.image_prompt: Summary slide with key takeaways presented as bullet points, possibly with a checkmark icon next to each.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Type a short sentence and observe **tokenization**.
Type a long, complex word and see how it breaks into multiple **tokens**.
slides.narration:
As an assignment, please do the following.
Find an online **tokenizer** tool.
Type a short sentence like "Hello, how are you today?".
Observe how it splits into **tokens**.
Then type a long, complex word.
See how it breaks into multiple **tokens**.
slides.image_prompt: Assignment slide with instructions, an icon of a computer screen, and a hand typing.
